verdict.rationale: Crossmint's agent-payment stack does embed some verifiable-identity mechanics — a delegated signer bound to a user-approved, onchain-enforced permission set, and card-network 'Agent Pay' recognition (Visa VIC/Mastercard Agent Pay) that flags a transaction as agent-initiated with scoped spend limits — which gives merchants indirect signal that a transaction is from an authorized, rule-bound agent rather than an anonymous actor. However, none of the evidence describes a merchant-facing registry, trust-tier system, or verifiable agent profile/signature merchants can inspect independently of the payment rails. Missing for 10: an explicit agent identity/credential merchants can query or verify, a trust-tier classification system, and any documentation framing this as a bot-vs-trusted-agent traffic signal rather than pure payment authorization.
